rationale: Matthew 8:20 is the first verse in this app's BSB text of Matthew to use "the Son of Man". Daniel 7:13 describes "One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven" (BSB). Later in Matthew, Jesus' own words take up Daniel's cloud imagery directly: "coming on the clouds of heaven" (24:30 and 26:64, BSB). At 8:20, though, nothing ties the phrase to Daniel except the phrase itself. There are no clouds, no dominion and no throne, only a man with "no place to lay His head". Scholars dispute what the phrase means on Jesus' lips. Craig Blomberg (excerpted by Redemption Seminary) reads a Danielic background behind even this saying, while calling it one of the sayings that "seem least dependent on a Danielic background." Geza Vermes (as reported by Alexander and Goodman) argued that the Aramaic bar nash could stand for "I" or for a human being in general, and that the idiomatic sayings have "a higher chance of being authentic" than the Danielic ones. That is why the type is motif: a phrase that recurs in Matthew and later takes up Daniel's wording (24:30; 26:64). Whether 8:20 already carries that content is the disputed point, and that is why the label is plausible, not strong: at this verse the link is debated, not stated.
